chunks: Hamzah ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alavi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim informed me, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Muawiyah ibn Wahab, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The Shias are three: one who is a true lover, and he is from us; one who adorns himself with us, and we are the adornment for whoever adorns himself with us; and one who attaches himself to us for worldly gain. And whoever attaches himself to us for worldly gain will be made poor.

key_terms.مُتَزَيِّنٌ بِنَا: One who adorns himself with us (using the Imams for status)
key_terms.مُحِبٌّ وَادٍ: A true/affectionate lover (implying deep, genuine love)
key_terms.مُسْتَأْكِلٌ بِنَا: One who attaches himself to us (for sustenance/gain)

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of Shia followers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to delineate the sociological reality of the Shia community, distinguishing between authentic devotion, performative piety (*mutazayyin*), and opportunistic materialism (*musta'kil*). This classification underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on sincerity (*ikhlas*) versus social climbing, warning that those who exploit the Ahl al-Bayt for worldly sustenance ultimately incur spiritual destitution.
